Heavy/long periods (menorrhagia) also supports chronic blood loss leading to iron-deficiency anemia. Forehead/bilateral temple pain could be from anemia-related headache, but we must also consider other causes (e.g., infection/neurologic), though melena + menorrhagia are most discriminating.
Top candidates:
1) Anemia — supported by melena + heavy/long menses + fatigue + presyncope.
2) Digestive Diseases (upper GI bleed) — black stools point to GI bleeding source causing anemia.
3) Circulatory Diseases — could contribute to dizziness, but melena/menorrhagia makes bleeding/anemia more likely.
4) Possible NSTEMI / STEMI or Unstable angina — dizziness can occur, but black stools and heavy menses are more specific for bleeding/anemia; still need to rule out cardiac ischemia if exertional symptoms/chest pain.
5) Panic attack — can cause lightheadedness, but melena/menorrhagia are not explained.
Most informative next question: determine severity/timing of bleeding and anemia clues—ask about any recent vomiting blood or abdominal pain, and whether stools are truly tarry/black.
